source_evidence: With a traditional 401(k), the tax benefit is upfront. With a Roth 401(k), the tax benefit comes later.
question: Misconception: Traditional and Roth 401(k) contributions are both taxed only when you withdraw the money.
answer: That is not quite right. Traditional 401(k) contributions and investment earnings are tax-deferred, so taxes are paid when the savings are withdrawn. Roth 401(k) contributions are made with after-tax dollars; account earnings and withdrawals are generally tax-free.
